title: ManhattanGrid: float classification drops last grid line on exact-multiple extents
description: _grid_size (mobility.py:794) uses int(floor((hi-lo)/spacing)); 0.3/0.1 == 2.999...9 -> grid_size 2, so snap_to_grid(0.3,0.3) returns (0.2,0.2) and the max bound is unreachable as a grid point. Fix with round() plus epsilon or decimal/Fraction-based extent math; test non-integer spacings where extent is an exact multiple.
close_reason: Fixed _grid_size (python/src/lichen/sim/mobility.py): float floor((hi-lo)/spacing) replaced with _exact_extent_cells, a decimal-exact floor via Fraction(repr(extent))/Fraction(repr(spacing)) - recovers decimal intent that binary floats lose (0.3/0.1 == 2.999...9), so exact-multiple extents keep the max bound reachable as a grid point while genuine partial cells (0.35/0.1) still floor. Chose Fraction(repr(...)) over the round()+epsilon alternative: no magic tolerance, deterministic for all decimal-intent extents. Test-first with independent oracle: test_snap_to_grid_exact_multiple_decimal_extent asserts _grid_size==3 and snapped max bound approx 0.3 (exact-multiple case, RED pre-fix: returned 0.2) plus the partial-cell guard (0.35 extent stays 3 cells, passes pre and post). tests/sim full suite: 1632 passed, 35 skipped. ruff + mypy clean on touched files. Committed.
